summary.headline: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 bids doubled available funding, prompting plans to scale back the project and seek Fall Town Meeting approval.
summary.summary: The Southborough Trails Committee met to welcome returning member Isabelle Murphy and address a significant budget shortfall for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail. Bids for the planned bridge and boardwalk across Stony Brook came in at roughly double the committee's available funds, leading members to explore constructing only the bridge and postponing the boardwalk. The committee also discussed closing out Phase 1, ongoing trail disruptions caused by National Grid power line construction, and approved funding for the summer Yoga on the Trails program.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee conducted opening roll call, welcomed Isabelle Murphy back to the committee following her re-appointment, deferred approval of meeting minutes, and adjourned at the end of the meeting.
key_details: All five committee members were present.
Isabelle Murphy was officially sworn in and welcomed back to the committee.
Approval of past meeting minutes was deferred to the next meeting.
topics.outcome: Meeting called to order at 6:00 PM and adjourned at 7:39 PM.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 1 project closeout and funding
topics.summary: The committee reviewed progress on Phase 1 of the Peninsula Trail, which recently saw the installation of new trailhead kiosks, interpretive signs, and paved accessible parking off Route 30 and Central Street. Members discussed closing out the Phase 1 Community Preservation Act project by June so an unspent balance of $47,000 can potentially be repurposed for Phase 2 at a future Town Meeting. The committee also discussed parking access issues, noting that a crosswalk connecting to Sanofi parking was deemed too expensive and complex due to road geometry and ADA requirements.
key_details: Phase 1 MassTrails grant work was completed with six signs installed and five parking spaces paved.
An unspent $47,000 in CPA funds remains in the Phase 1 account.
Town counsel advised that Phase 1 must be formally closed out before asking Town Meeting to reallocate the remaining funds to Phase 2.
Plans for a crosswalk across Route 30 to Sanofi parking were abandoned due to prohibitive costs for three required crosswalks and ADA sidewalks.
The committee hopes to finalize closeout documentation and presentation materials by June.
topics.outcome: The committee agreed to prepare a CPA sign, complete closeout paperwork, and prepare a presentation for the Community Preservation Committee.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 bid results and shortfall
topics.summary: Phase 2 construction bids for a bridge and boardwalk crossing Stony Brook to connect to the Bay Circuit Trail came in at $445,000 and $468,000, roughly double the available funding of about $211,000. Due to structural requirements, the bridge cannot be built from cheaper wood, so the committee discussed omitting the boardwalk and building only the bridge first. Because the scope and funding structure would change, the committee plans to ask voters at a Fall Special Town Meeting to modify the project approval and transfer the $47,000 from Phase 1, with plans to seek a MassTrails grant in February 2027.
key_details: Two bids were submitted for Phase 2 construction, ranging from $445,000 to $468,000.
The committee has approximately $211,000 available in CPA funds including contingency.
Cost estimates suggest the bridge represents about 65% of the total cost and the boardwalk about 35%.
A wooden bridge was ruled out because required abutment heights and engineering constraints make it unfeasible.
A planned volunteer trail-building day with AMC and Bay Circuit Trail volunteers on Earth Day was postponed due to a lack of signups.
topics.outcome: The committee decided to explore bidding or pricing the bridge separately and prepare a proposal for the Fall Special Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The bridge project is the key missing link connecting Southborough trails across Stony Brook to the regional Bay Circuit Trail, but cannot proceed without additional funding or scope reductions voted by Town Meeting.

topics.title: National Grid transmission line work and trail safety
topics.summary: National Grid is conducting extensive utility pole replacement work along Southborough trails, placing heavy timber mats that will remain in place for up to a year into early 2027. Following an incident where a trail user injured an ankle on the mats, the company agreed to provide 10 larger warning signs cautioning the public to travel at their own risk. The committee decided against closing the trails, planning instead to distribute safety flyers at Annual Town Meeting and provide public updates via social media.
key_details: National Grid pole replacement work will impact trail corridors across town through early 2027.
Timber construction mats may be removed temporarily in summer but could remain until November.
National Grid will install 10 warning signs along affected trails, and the committee will print safety notices for Town Meeting.
Temporary short-term trail closures of a day or two will occur when utility wires are actively being pulled.
The committee is asking whether National Grid can leave a gravel service road in place after construction to improve trail footing.
topics.outcome: The committee agreed to post warning notices, coordinate signage with National Grid, and request advance notices of temporary wire-pulling closures.

topics.title: Yoga on the Trails program funding
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the community Yoga on the Trails program run by instructor Emma Bartolini. Because the Trails Committee annual operating budget will decrease from $4,250 to $1,750 in FY27 due to the removal of trail mowing costs, members voted to allocate $300 for four monthly sessions from July through October. Returning member Isabelle Murphy volunteered to manage the Eventbrite ticketing system.
key_details: The Trails Committee annual operating budget will drop to $1,750 for FY27.
Yoga on the Trails sessions cost $75 per session paid to the instructor.
The program is free to residents and held at the field on Parkerville Road.
The committee voted to authorize $300 to cover four sessions in the upcoming fiscal year.
topics.outcome: The committee voted unanimously (5-0) to approve $300 from the FY27 budget for four Yoga on the Trails sessions.

topics.title: Potential 9/11 Field trail connector to Marlborough
topics.summary: A committee member proposed scouting a potential trail link from the existing 9/11 Field trail loop along a waterway to connect with Marlborough's trail network. The member will walk the path, map it using GPS tools, and determine whether the Department of Conservation and Recreation would permit formal trail establishment. The committee also discussed winter parking and plowing access at town trailheads.
key_details: Fishermen have already created an informal path leading toward Marlborough trails near an existing small bridge.
A committee member will scout and flag the proposed route and map it on AllTrails.
The committee will consult DCR regarding land permissions before any trail work begins.
Members discussed asking DPW to plow winter access for two or three key trailhead parking locations next winter.
topics.outcome: The member will scout and map the route and report findings back to the committee at a future meeting.

votes.motion: Approve $300 out of the committee budget for Yoga on the Trails sessions.

upcoming.what: Special Town Meeting consideration of Peninsula Trail Phase 2 scope and funding transfer
